practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution outlines the appointment, tenure, and removal of the Chief Minister and other Ministers of a State?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 164 deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister by the Governor and the appointment of other ministers on the advice of the Chief Minister. Article 163 deals with the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor. Article 166 is about the conduct of business of the state government. Article 167 specifies duties of the Chief Minister.

practiceQuestions.q: Who administers the oath of office and secrecy to the members of the State Council of Ministers?
opts: The Chief Justice of the concerned High Court
The Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 164(3), before a minister enters upon his office, the Governor administers to him the oaths of office and of secrecy. Distractor A is incorrect as the High Court Chief Justice administers the oath to the Governor, not the ministers.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary constitutional role of the Chief Minister in relation to the Governor and the Council of Ministers?
opts: He acts as the sole channel of communication between them.
He appoints the Governor with the consent of the President.
He has the power to veto ordinances passed by the Governor.
He is directly responsible for presiding over meetings of the State Legislative Council.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 167 designates the Chief Minister as the principal channel of communication between the Council of Ministers and the Governor. All decisions of the CoM relating to administration and proposals for legislation must be communicated to the Governor through the CM.

practiceQuestions.q: According to the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003, what is the maximum permissible strength of the Council of Ministers in a state, including the Chief Minister?
opts: 10 percent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly
15 percent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly
15 members fixed uniformly for all states
One-third of the total members of the Legislative Council
practiceQuestions.sol: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 added Article 164(1A) which states that the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers in a State shall not exceed 15 percent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly of that State (with a minimum limit of 12 ministers).

practiceQuestions.q: If a person is not a member of either House of the State Legislature at the time of appointment as a minister, for how long can they remain a minister without being elected?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 164(4), a minister who for any period of six consecutive months is not a member of the Legislature of the State shall at the expiration of that period cease to be a minister. This applies to the Chief Minister as well.

practiceQuestions.q: Which article establishes that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor in the exercise of their functions?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 163(1) states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor in the exercise of his functions, except insofar as he is by or under the constitution required to exercise his functions in his discretion.

practiceQuestions.q: The salaries and allowances of the Chief Minister and other state ministers are determined by whom?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 164(5), the salaries and allowances of ministers shall be such as the Legislature of the State may from time to time by law determine and, until the Legislature of the State so determines, shall be as specified in the Second Schedule.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the Chief Minister submit their resignation if they wish to step down from office?
opts: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
The Chief Justice of the High Court
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor and tenders his resignation to the Governor. The resignation of the Chief Minister means the automatic resignation of the entire Council of Ministers, as the CM is the head of the CoM.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies/councils is the Chief Minister NOT a member or chairman of?
opts: State Planning Board / State Development Council
Zonal Council (serves as Vice-Chairman by rotation)
practiceQuestions.sol: The Prime Minister is the Chairman of the National Development Council (NDC) and NITI Aayog, not the Chief Minister. CMs are members of the NDC, Governing Council of NITI Aayog, Inter-State Council (chaired by PM), and serve as Vice-Chairman of Zonal Councils by rotation.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Governor dismiss a minister on the recommendation of the Chief Minister?
opts: No, only the State Legislative Assembly can remove a minister.
Yes, the Governor must dismiss a minister if the CM so recommends.
Only with the prior concurrence of the President of India.
No, ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor independently of the CM.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 164(2), ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor. However, this 'pleasure' is exercised by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister. If a minister disagrees with the CM or fails to cooperate, the CM can ask them to resign or recommend their dismissal to the Governor.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the principle of collective responsibility operate within the State Council of Ministers under Article 164(2)?
opts: Ministers are individually responsible to the Governor for their respective departmental actions.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly.
The Chief Minister alone is responsible to the Parliament for state governance.
Ministers are collectively responsible to the High Court of the state.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 164(2) explicitly states that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State. This means all ministers swim and sink together; a vote of no-confidence against one minister or the CM results in the fall of the entire CoM.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional implication if the Chief Minister resigns or dies while in office?
opts: The senior-most cabinet minister automatically becomes the Chief Minister.
President's Rule (Article 356) is immediately imposed in the state.
The Council of Ministers automatically stands dissolved, creating a vacuum until a new CM is sworn in.
The Governor assumes direct executive control with the help of the Chief Secretary.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chief Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers. The demise or resignation of the CM dissolves the CoM automatically, because the CoM cannot exist without its head. Other ministers cannot function independently without a CM.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of the discretionary powers of the Governor under Article 163, what happens when no single political party secures a clear majority in the State Legislative Assembly?
opts: The Governor must dissolve the assembly and order fresh elections immediately.
The Governor exercises personal judgment in appointing the Chief Minister to form a stable government.
The President appoints the Chief Minister based on Union Cabinet advice.
The outgoing Chief Minister remains in office indefinitely until a majority is won.
practiceQuestions.sol: When a hung assembly occurs, the Governor exercises conditional discretion in appointing the Chief Minister. Usually, the leader of the single largest party or pre-poll alliance is invited to prove majority within a stipulated timeframe.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Chief Minister's role differ from that of the Prime Minister regarding internal cabinet management?
opts: The CM has absolute power over ministers, whereas the PM has limited advisory powers.
Both operate under identical constitutional constraints, but the CM's political clout is often constrained by state-level factionalism and coalition dynamics.
The CM cannot reshuffle portfolios without the Governor's written concurrence.
The CM has no say in portfolio allocation; it is done strictly by the Governor.
practiceQuestions.sol: Surgically speaking, structurally the CM and PM play analogous roles ('first among equals'). However, in practice, state politics often exhibits volatile coalition dynamics, regional satraps, and high factionalism, making the CM's control over the cabinet sometimes more delicate than that of the PM.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Article 167, what is the nature of the Governor's right to seek information from the Chief Minister?
opts: It is a constitutional obligation of the CM to furnish such information as the Governor may call for relating to state administration and legislation.
It is merely a convention and has no binding legal basis in the Constitution.
The Governor can only seek information regarding financial matters approved by the Speaker.
The CM can refuse to answer if the information pertains to internal party affairs.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 167(b) specifically commands that it is the duty of the Chief Minister to furnish such information relating to the administration of the affairs of the state and proposals for legislation as the Governor may call for. This is a mandatory constitutional duty, not discretionary.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional significance of Article 163(2) regarding the Governor's discretion?
opts: It states that the Governor's decision on whether a matter falls within his discretion is final and cannot be questioned in court.
It gives the Chief Minister absolute veto power over any discretionary action of the Governor.
It requires the Supreme Court to validate all discretionary actions prior to execution.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 163(2) provides that if any question arises whether any matter is or is not a matter as respects which the Governor is by or under this Constitution required to act in his discretion, the decision of the Governor in his discretion shall be final, and the validity of anything done by the Governor shall not be called in question on the ground that he ought or ought not to have acted in his discretion.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Chief Minister referred to as the 'keystone of the cabinet arch'?
opts: Because without his approval, no minister can communicate with the judiciary.
Because he holds the power to create, sustain, and destroy the cabinet structure; if he falls, the entire arch collapses.
Because he is appointed directly by the Supreme Court of India.
Because he alone represents the state in international treaties.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sir Ivor Jennings used this metaphor for the Prime Minister, and it applies equally to the Chief Minister at the state level. The CM coordinates, commands, and controls the government. If the CM resigns, the arch (Council of Ministers) falls apart.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a member of the State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) be appointed as the Chief Minister?
opts: No, the Chief Minister must compulsorily be a directly elected member of the Legislative Assembly.
Yes, a member of the Legislative Council can be appointed as Chief Minister, as seen with several historical examples in India.
Only with the special permission of the Election Commission of India.
Only if the Legislative Assembly passes a unanimous resolution consenting to it.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution does not bar a member of the Legislative Council from becoming a Chief Minister. For instance, leaders like C. Rajagopalachari, M. Karunanidhi, Nitish Kumar, and Yogi Adityanath (at various points/states) have been members of the Upper House or appointed while being members. (Note: Yogi Adityanath was MLC when appointed in UP in 2017).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the relationship between the Governor's power to grant pardons (Article 161) and the advice of the State Council of Ministers?
opts: The Governor exercises the pardon power entirely on his personal whim without consulting the CoM.
The Governor must act on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the CM, similar to the President's exercise under Article 72.
The power of pardon vests exclusively in the Chief Minister, who advises the Governor accordingly.
The Governor can only grant pardons on the direct order of the Supreme Court.
practiceQuestions.sol: Like the President under Article 72, the Governor under Article 161 exercises the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister, as established by constitutional jurisprudence (e.g., Supreme Court rulings on state remission cases).

practiceQuestions.q: How does the size and hierarchy of the State Council of Ministers typically manifest in practice?
opts: All ministers belong to a single uniform rank with equal salaries and cabinet privileges.
It is a three-tier body consisting of Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers, though not all tiers are mandatory.
It consists solely of Cabinet Ministers appointed by the High Court.
The Constitution rigidly mandates that every state must have exactly 3 Cabinet Ministers and 2 Ministers of State.
practiceQuestions.sol: Though the Constitution simply uses the term 'Council of Ministers', politically and administratively it follows the British parliamentary model: Cabinet Ministers (who head important departments), Ministers of State (independent charge or attached), and Deputy Ministers (assisting).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief Minister and the State Executive:
1. The Constitution of India contains a specific procedure for the selection and election of the Chief Minister.
2. A person who is not a member of the State Legislature can be appointed as Chief Minister for a maximum period of six months without being elected.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Constitution does not contain any specific procedure for the selection and appointment of the Chief Minister. Article 164 simply says 'The Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Governor and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.' Statement 2 is correct because Article 164(4) permits a non-legislator to be a minister (including CM) for 6 months, within which they must get elected to either House of the State Legislature.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Council of Ministers in a State:
1. The total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers in a State shall not exceed 15 percent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly of that State.
2. There is a constitutional provision prescribing a minimum number of 15 ministers in every State Council of Ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct in stating the 15 percent ceiling (added by 91st Amendment Act, 2003). However, Statement 2 is incorrect because the minimum number of ministers (including CM) is prescribed as 12, not 15. Thus, Statement 2 is wrong.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 167 of the Indian Constitution:
1. It defines the duties of the Chief Minister with respect to furnishing information to the Governor.
2. The Governor can directly issue orders to individual departments bypassing the Chief Minister, as the Chief Minister is not the sole executive head.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Article 167 outlines the CM's duty to communicate all decisions of the CoM and administrative proposals to the Governor. Statement 2 is incorrect because rules of business and constitutional conventions dictate that the Governor cannot bypass the Chief Minister and issue direct orders to individual ministers or departments without violating collective responsibility and the CM's leadership role.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the tenure and removal of ministers in a state:
1. Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.
2. The Governor can dismiss a minister on their own initiative without any recommendation from the Chief Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct as per Article 164(2). Statement 2 is incorrect because while ministers hold office during the Governor's pleasure, the 'pleasure' of the Governor is exercised constitutionally on the advice of the Chief Minister. The Governor cannot arbitrarily dismiss a minister independently of the CM's advice, as it would destroy cabinet cohesion.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the State Council of Ministers:
1. The council remains in office as long as it enjoys the confidence of the State Legislative Assembly.
2. Individual ministers can be members of either the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council or even non-legislators temporarily.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Statement 1 reflects the principle of collective responsibility to the Legislative Assembly under Article 164(2). Statement 2 correctly reflects that ministers can be drawn from the Assembly, Council, or be non-legislators who must get elected within 6 months.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the Chief Minister:
1. The Chief Minister recommends persons who can be appointed as ministers by the Governor.
2. The Chief Minister allocates and reshuffles portfolios among the ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Governor can appoint only those persons as ministers who are recommended by the CM (Article 164). Furthermore, the allocation and reshuffling of portfolios among ministers is the exclusive prerogative of the Chief Minister.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional position of the Governor vis-a-vis the Council of Ministers:
1. The Governor can act entirely independently of the Council of Ministers in all matters relating to state administration.
2. Article 163 requires the Governor to act on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers except in matters where they are required to act in their discretion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Governor is a constitutional head and must act on ministerial advice in all normal executive matters. Statement 2 is correct as Article 163 explicitly establishes that the Governor acts on aid and advice, except in specified discretionary domains.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal or resignation of the Council of Ministers:
1. The resignation or death of the Chief Minister automatically dissolves the Council of Ministers.
2. Passing a vote of no-confidence in the Legislative Assembly against a single minister results in the resignation of only that specific minister, leaving the rest of the cabinet untouched.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; the CM is the head of the CoM, and their exit dissolves the body. Statement 2 is incorrect because due to 'collective responsibility' (Article 164(2)), the Council of Ministers is a single entity; a no-confidence motion or defeat on a major policy applies to the entire CoM, meaning the whole cabinet must resign, not just one minister.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of the Chief Minister vis-a-vis the State Legislature:
1. The Chief Minister advises the Governor with regard to summoning and proroguing the sessions of the State Legislature.
2. The Chief Minister can recommend the dissolution of the Legislative Assembly to the Governor at any time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Chief Minister plays a pivotal legislative role by advising the Governor on summoning, proroguing the legislature, and can also recommend the premature dissolution of the Legislative Assembly, leading to fresh elections.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the oath and legal immunity of state ministers:
1. Ministers take the oath of office and secrecy administered by the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
2. The Constitution of India contains provisions for legal immunity for official acts and proceedings of the state legislature similar to Parliamentary privileges.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because oaths of office and secrecy to ministers are administered by the Governor, not the Speaker. Statement 2 is correct because Article 194 provides privileges, immunities, and powers to the state legislature and its members, analogous to parliamentary privileges under Article 105.
